absent: Architecture breakpoint operation effects, register handling and exception vector meanings.
Allocation, capacity and lifetime of shared print buffer, prompt storage and grep search storage.
Full debugger flag set, numeric values and initial state.
Console write implementation, loglevel constants and kernel log interaction guarantees.
Debug transport operations, packet buffer capacity and flush semantics.
Poll function table population, ordering and full return-value contract.
Module symbol iteration, symbol data locking and lifetime.
Environment table capacity, persistence and concurrent mutation rules.
Register block layout and error code semantics passed to architecture exception handling.
Initial value and full ordering semantics of print ownership marker and activity counter.

findings.text: Exposes a breakpoint helper that brackets an architecture-provided breakpoint operation with ordering assurances on entry and exit while maintaining a balanced activity count around the trap.

Provides variadic debugger display formatting through a shared central routine that attributes a message source, fans out to consoles, optionally mirrors to the kernel log, and integrates filtering and paging.
Provides host-bound console transport by encoding text as hexadecimal inside output packets and splitting longer messages into bounded pieces that respect packet buffer limits.

Provides reliable packet emission with checksum protection and acknowledgment-driven retransmission, treating an unexpected packet start as a reconnect indication and tolerating an interrupt character while awaiting acknowledgment.
Provides alternative blocking receive waits, one polling a table of input functions with support for replaying a staged buffer and one repeatedly querying a single debug transport until data arrives.

Provides single-character acquisition from polled inputs with duplicate newline suppression after carriage return, source-change tolerance, bounded escape disambiguation, and translation of terminal sequences into control codes.

Provides prompt-driven line acquisition with cursor motion, insertion and deletion, history signalling, symbol-name completion with truncation notice, and detection of sequences that transfer control to remote debugging.
Provides environment lookup by name with strict terminator checking plus integer decoding wrappers that distinguish missing names from missing values and malformed numbers.

Provides sequential kernel symbol enumeration that skips nameless entries together with prefix completion that counts matches and extends the caller prefix toward the longest common match within limits.
Provides transfer between line-oriented debugging and stub-driven remote debugging by forwarding command buffers to stub state handling and recognizing stub framing inside typed input.
Breakpoint helper acts as an externally reachable trap entry that advertises setup activity for the duration of the underlying architecture breakpoint.
Variadic print routine acts as the primary externally reachable display and logging entry for debugger-generated messages.

Central formatted output is serialized by suppressing local interrupts during the critical section and by acquiring ownership of a shared marker, with same-owner re-entry permitted and release performed with ordering before interrupts are restored.

Output geometry, logging enablement and completion listing limits are governed by environment tunables with safe defaults when absent or invalid, and returned length reflects the full formatted content independent of later filtering or paging decisions.

Stored symbol names use length-prefixed records with periodic markers for efficient seeking and an extended length form for large names, while iteration advances monotonically and delegates beyond-core positions to separate module handling.

Symbol iteration cursor as observed carries a name area with offset, a logical position, and auxiliary end markers for extended ranges, reinitialized to empty name and recomputed offset whenever repositioned.

Paged display accumulates line counts including wrapped columns and, upon reaching the page height, presents a pause prompt where quit aborts and clears paging, page or line inputs resume with temporary filter suspension, and search enters interactive lookup.

Filtering accumulates formatted bytes until a line boundary, tests the completed line for a substring, discards non-matching lines by shifting remaining bytes forward, and treats prompt output specially to leave filtering.

Stub state handling selects behavior from the leading command character, delegating exception commands to architecture handling, staging step and continue commands for later processing, priming replay for framed commands, and otherwise acknowledging while emitting any pending response.

Debugger mode uses bit flags for paging, command interruption and transitions between transparent pass-through and remote operation, tested and set through dedicated macros at print, input and transition points.

Pause-prompt interaction re-enters formatted output while ownership is still held, so correct same-owner re-entry and careful management of shared buffer cursors are required to avoid deadlock, interleaving or loss of pending filtered bytes.

Character polling loops indefinitely over input sources with periodic watchdog maintenance and delay-based escape resolution, so a non-responsive source or mistimed escape window can stall input or misclassify escape sequences.

Paging defaults to twenty four lines and eighty columns when tunables are missing or non-positive, logging defaults to disabled, completion listing threshold defaults to thirty entries, and paging and search prompts have overridable textual defaults.

Escape decoding assigns up to sixteen, down to fourteen, right to six, left to two, home to one, deletion to four and end to five, with the line editor interpreting those values for movement and history.
Escape disambiguation waits with a one thousand microsecond granularity up to an overall window corresponding to two seconds before treating escape as a lone key.

Packet exchange uses dollar to open and hash to introduce a two-digit hexadecimal checksum, plus for acknowledgment, minus for negative acknowledgment, O to mark console output packets, and handles control interrupt during acknowledgment wait.
